items.gist: The prāṇa course runs thirty-six aṅgulas from heart to nose-tip, and its vigor, strength, and motion are the same in all bodies.
The thirty-six-aṅgula course contains paired ingoing and outgoing movements; tuṭi, caṣaka, nāḍī, horātra, and prahara measures are defined.
Sandhyās, Ketu, Rāhu, and other grahas are related to praharas, with siddhi, mokṣa, bhoga, and other results.
Nakṣatras, tattvas, Bhairavas, and Śaktis arise in sequence; cruel and gentle actions occur by day and night, and mukti comes at their junction through vyāpti, dhyāna, and yoga.
Dharma and adharma diminish through dīkṣā, vyāpti, dhyāna, and yoga; an ahorātra in prāṇa-course is called a month.
Kṛṣṇa and Śukla pakṣas, tithis, and viśrāma are correlated with prakāśa and saṃvit in the day-night division.
The duration of a moment depends on the clarity of saṃvit; day is the knower's abiding and night is the object's rest.
Jāgrat, svapna, suṣupti, and turya are discussed, along with the unequal length of day and night in bodies and cities.
The Triyambaka lineage explains the day-night division from the heart; the unawakened place is questioned as a true day.
In Kṛṣṇapakṣa the moon loses kalās near dvādaśānta and enters the prāṇa-sun at amāvāsyā.
The body is filled and dissolved through sun and moon; fifteen kalās wane, while the sixteenth is not lost, and pakṣasandhi is defined.
Saṃdhi, sūryagraha, the moon's nectar, and Rāhu as māyā-pramātā are explained.
The union of sun and moon is the great graha; even without amāvāsyā it can occur, and mokṣa is distant when the moon is half-absorbed.
Between grāsa and mokṣa, bathing, meditation, homa, and japa yield worldly and otherworldly fruits; tithiccheda brings loss and gain.
The consciousness-sun enters the nectar-moon and fills it kalā by kalā; fifteen tuṭis become tithis in the bright fortnight.
The month is restated; uttarāyaṇa, viṣuva, and dakṣiṇāyana are correlated with the sun's entry into zodiac signs.
Birth, growth, decline, and other states arise from Makara onward; zodiacal entries yield corresponding karmic fruits.
